The Data Science Center turns UCLA's raw research data into usable,
reproducible science, through direct research support, hands-on training,
and stewardship of shared infrastructure, reaching researchers and students
across most of UCLA's schools and divisions.

## Four findings (2017-2024 evidence period, except where noted)

**1. Reach spans nearly every part of campus, not one department.** Of
1,575 UCLA-affiliated workshop-attendance records, 838 are mapped to a
known school, division, or institute; the remainder are recorded but
lack department information, not concentrated in one unresolved bucket
(`claim-register.md` #7).

**2. Direct, one-on-one research support is substantial on its own.** DSC
and DataSquad recorded 741 direct consultations from 2023 through 2025
(LibInsight scheduled appointments combined with DataSquad walk-in
sign-ins, canceled appointments excluded). This is a count of interactions,
not unique people, and covers 2023-2025 only (`claim-register.md` #6).

**3. Training builds capacity that outlasts the workshop.** Public evidence
confirms at least 39 people who came through DSC-supported UC Carpentries
workshops (2021-2025) were subsequently observed in research or
data-intensive roles. This is an early trajectory signal, not a
representative tracer study; role-start dates were not verified, so this
shows association, not that DSC caused the outcome (`claim-register.md`
#3-5).

**4. Shared infrastructure is doing real, cited work.** UCLA Dataverse,
which DSC operates, holds 377 published datasets and 25,330 files, with
143,414 recorded downloads. At least 13 linked publications have drawn 258
citations so far (`infrastructure.qmd`, live KPI).

## One case

**Carceral Ecologies** (UCLA Institute for Society and Genetics). DSC and
DataSquad provided multi-year research support, including R server
infrastructure, data processing, and student training, for a
helicopter-surveillance dataset. For one documented processing task, an
approximately 159-fold runtime reduction was observed under the reported
conditions. The research drew national media coverage (Los Angeles Times,
The New Yorker, Bloomberg) and DSC-trained a research student in
sustainable R workflows along the way (`claim-register.md` #1).

## Evidence, periods, and units

| Finding | Source | Period | Unit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Department/division reach | Org-parent crosswalk (tested) | 2017-2024 | Attendee-event record |
| Direct consultations (741) | Consultation audit, combined + deduped | 2023-2025 | Consultation record |
| Trajectory signal (39) | Named-people identity passes, deduped | 2021-2025 attendance | Person, public confirmation |
| Dataverse metrics | Dataverse API + OpenAlex | Cumulative to date | Dataset / file / download / citation |
| Case study | Impact case-study log | Multi-year engagement | Documented engagement |

: Full paths and methods for each row are in `claim-register.md`.

## Limitations

- **Instruction data covers 2017-2024 only** in the current published
  aggregate; 5,722 of 15,765 total workshop-attendance records have
  unknown UCLA affiliation and are excluded from the reach finding above,
  not treated as non-UCLA.
- **The trajectory finding is not a tracer study.** No pass captured a
  role-start date, so a confirmed later role does not establish it began
  after DSC engagement. Coverage is not exhaustive or systematically
  re-verified.
- **The consultations figure (741) covers 2023-2025 only**, not DSC's
  full history, and counts interaction records, not unique people. It
  comes from a separate, narrower reconciliation than the one behind the
  instruction and trajectory findings above, and the two have not been
  merged onto one consistent timeline yet.
- **One case study is illustrative, not representative** of the full
  range of DSC's work; a broader case set covering instruction and
  infrastructure engagements specifically is in progress.
